s1.syndrome_frame: Painful erosive skin lesion around a stoma site following abdominal surgery
salient_findings: Painful, erosive lesion around the stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
Epidermal erosion with suprabasal epidermal splitting and acantholysis on histopathology
Intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis on direct immunofluorescence
key_facts: Patient has a 10-year history of Crohn disease
Patient underwent total proctocolectomy and ileostomy
Symptoms developed 5 weeks after surgery
Lesion is painful and erosive
No additional cutaneous or mucosal lesions are present
Microbiological cultures were negative
Histopathology showed suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis
Direct immunofluorescence showed intercellular deposition of IgG and C3
High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3

differentials: Mucous membrane pemphigoid with anti-β4 antibodies
per_call: Mucous membrane pemphigoid with anti-β4 antibodies

shortlist.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3, and histopathology showing suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Painful erosive lesion and presence of autoantibodies, although less likely due to lack of associated neoplasm

shortlist.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Autoantibodies against desmoglein 1, but less likely due to lack of characteristic histopathological findings

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of autoantibodies and blistering disease, although less likely due to atypical histopathological findings

shortlist.label: Stoma-related pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Painful erosive lesion around stoma site, although less likely due to lack of characteristic histopathological findings and presence of autoantibodies

raw.rationale: The presence of suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis, intercellular deposition of IgG and C3, and high levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 are characteristic of Pemphigus vulgaris

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: Typically associated with underlying neoplasms, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
rejected.why: Characterized by autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 only, and typically involves the skin without mucosal involvement

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: Characterized by subepidermal blistering and linear IgG and C3 deposition along the basement membrane, which is not consistent with the histopathology findings

rejected.label: Stoma-related pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: Typically presents with ulcerative lesions and does not have the characteristic immunofluorescence or autoantibody profile of Pemphigus vulgaris
